fatal_errors: The proposed experiment uses identical PGM loadings on both supports, so it cannot establish that PGM consumption can be reduced.

The cited evidence concerns essentially PGM-free CO oxidation over spinel powders, not PGM layers under multicomponent automotive exhaust; the claimed suppression of PGM sintering and preservation of NOx activity are unsupported extrapolations.
The stated 500–800 °C synthesis range conflicts with the cited preparation at 900 °C for 4 h, and the exhaust ageing and reaction conditions are insufficiently specified.
explanation: This is not a reconstruction of the target intervention, which was a closed-loop high-throughput and machine-learning campaign optimizing multielement alloy composition and solvothermal processing based on post-ageing activity. It instead proposes a scientifically plausible high-entropy spinel-support strategy. The evidence directly supports lower CO-oxidation T10 and improved 14 h stability as metal diversity increases from four to seven elements, but it does not validate reduced PGM loading, ultra-thin PGM stabilization, NOx conversion, or realistic exhaust durability. The four-metal comparison is reasonable for isolating configurational-disorder effects, yet a conventional automotive catalyst and a lower-PGM high-entropy catalyst are needed to test the stated application. The experiment could discriminate support effects, but equal PGM loading and a vague exhaust protocol leave the central PGM-reduction claim untested. Its falsification rule is also unnecessarily rigid because requiring both a greater-than-50% T10 improvement and better stability could reject useful, statistically credible gains.
